summary.en-US: Send selected tabs, and optionally your sign-in, between your own browsers. End-to-end encrypted, peer-to-peer WebRTC, no central server.

description.en-US: Narada (named after Narada Muni, the messenger sage of the Bhagavata Purana) moves tabs between your browsers, including Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Brave and other combinations. How it works • Pair two browsers once with a one-time code, then confirm a 6-digit number shown on both. • Pick tabs and send them. Optionally include their cookies and site storage so you stay signed in. • The other browser shows exactly what arrived and which sites it would sign you in to. Nothing is applied until you accept. Private by design • Peer-to-peer: after a short encrypted handshake over public Nostr relays, the browsers talk directly over WebRTC (Google STUN only, no TURN). No server sits in the data path, and no account is needed. • End-to-end encrypted, with authentication by pinned device keys and forward secrecy. • Collects nothing: no analytics, no tracking, no developer servers. • The cookie and all-sites permissions are optional and requested only when you first send or accept sign-in data. Docs: https://dmdhrumilmistry.github.io/narada/docs.html · Source code: https://github.com/dmdhrumilmistry/narada
